body:
## Problem and selected delivery

The Documentation Center **Build** relationship picker (`artifactType=Release`) must keep the same candidate membership while the operator loads successive pages. Currently a newly committed build that sorts after the cursor can enter a continuation even though it was absent when page one was read.

**Selected as one focused GLM implementation task after #1048 and #1054 are fully accepted and closed.** Do not combine it with #1047, #1023, CI-efficiency/reliability investigations, or the #509 qualification umbrella. Recommended priority: **P2 correctness**.

## Verified source baseline and scope correction

Reviewed protected `main` **`c2602d9360af27a333d789b379d379d66d08ff42`** on September 20, 2026. This is read-only planning evidence; no runtime reproduction, implementation, migration execution or passing test is claimed.

- [ManagedDocumentEndpoints.cs](https://github.com/AeroLinkDEV/requirements-management-tool/blob/c2602d9360af27a333d789b379d379d66d08ff42/product/src/AeroLink.Api/ManagedDocumentEndpoints.cs#L814): `LinkOptionsAsync` carries `snapshotAt`, but the Release branch applies only Project/search, canonical sort key, continuation and `Take(pageSize + 1)`. It applies no membership-snapshot predicate.
- [ProgramRecord.cs](https://github.com/AeroLinkDEV/requirements-management-tool/blob/c2602d9360af27a333d789b379d379d66d08ff42/product/src/AeroLink.Domain/Programs/ProgramRecord.cs#L52): `SoftwareRelease` has no creation timestamp. Its random Guid, version, canonical identity, predecessor, released flag and nullable `ReleasedAt` are not creation/commit-order watermarks. `SoftwareBuild` is a different persistence entity and its `RecordedAt` does not cover all picker candidates.
- [SoftwareReleaseOrderingQuery.cs](https://github.com/AeroLinkDEV/requirements-management-tool/blob/c2602d9360af27a333d789b379d379d66d08ff42/product/src/AeroLink.Infrastructure/Persistence/SoftwareReleaseOrderingQuery.cs) already supplies canonical numeric order, historical-text handling and a stable ID tie-breaker. Preserve it.
- [ManagedDocumentPaging.cs](https://github.com/AeroLinkDEV/requirements-management-tool/blob/c2602d9360af27a333d789b379d379d66d08ff42/product/src/AeroLink.Api/ManagedDocumentPaging.cs) currently uses a v1 base64 JSON cursor. Release includes `canonical-release-order-v1` in its filter key. Encoding is not authentication; authorization is rechecked at the route. Changing the shared cursor must preserve other consumers.
- [ManagedDocumentApiTests.BuildIdentity.cs](https://github.com/AeroLinkDEV/requirements-management-tool/blob/c2602d9360af27a333d789b379d379d66d08ff42/product/tests/AeroLink.Api.Tests/ManagedDocumentApiTests.BuildIdentity.cs) checks canonical numeric paging and changed-filter/invalid-cursor rejection. It does not insert concurrent builds.
- [MANAGED_DOCUMENTATION_CENTER.md](https://github.com/AeroLinkDEV/requirements-management-tool/blob/c2602d9360af27a333d789b379d379d66d08ff42/product/docs/MANAGED_DOCUMENTATION_CENTER.md#L98) already records the Release exception explicitly. The opening claim in the original issue that documentation unconditionally promises Release snapshots is therefore superseded by this qualified statement.
- #1041 is now **closed as completed**. Refresh that state and current test tooling when implementation starts; the September 15 comment's outstanding dependency is historical.

This was found during #1037 / PR #1038 review and predates those changes. Numeric ordering and bounded keyset paging were corrected there; they do not freeze candidate membership.

## Required semantics

Define a precise database visibility boundary during page one's successful request. The eligible, committed release IDs at that boundary, in the authorized Project and normalized search scope, are the candidates for that continuation. A later insertion must not enter it, whether its display sort position is before or after the current cursor. Restarting at page one obtains a new boundary and can show the new build.

The guarantee covers **candidate membership and stable paging order**. It does not freeze current lifecycle labels or authorization forever. Recheck access on every page and when a selected relationship is written; revoked access must fail closed. Preserve exact Release IDs and canonical relationship/deep-link behavior.

A transaction that is not yet visible at the established boundary must not leak into later pages after committing. A short serialization fence may delay establishing page one's boundary until a competing writer completes; document and test that ordering. Do not hold a database transaction or connection open across browser requests.

## Design constraints and review decision

The September 15 suggestion to add nullable `CreatedAt` is a proposal, not an accepted schema decision. A constructor timestamp, `now()` default, or bare maximum sequence does **not by itself** handle late commits. PostgreSQL statement visibility and sequence allocation have different semantics; see [transaction isolation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/transaction-iso.html) and [sequence functions](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/functions-sequence.html).

Preferred design to evaluate at Astra checkpoint A: a small immutable **operational insertion watermark**, separate from controlled build identity and historical dates, with writer allocation and first-page boundary capture serialized consistently. Existing `ProjectControlledWriteScope` provides a relevant provider-aware locking precedent. It is not proof that all release writers currently use that scope.

1. Identify every writer: normal release creation, legacy import acceptance, fresh/resumed project completion, repositories, showcase creation/upgrades and relevant bulk/provider paths.
2. If selecting an ordinal/fence design, allocate only after the coordinating lock is held and retain that lock until commit. Page one captures the committed cutoff under the compatible fence. Continuations filter membership before canonical ordering and `Take`. A sequence default allocated before the lock is not sufficient. Cover existing project-lock order, newly created projects, rollback, cancellation and concurrent multi-writer behavior.
3. Prefer additive operational metadata. Existing rows may enter a documented pre-upgrade cohort without inventing their creation dates or historical order. New writes must not acquire that legacy exemption. Preserve IDs, raw Version, CanonicalIdentity, predecessor, lifecycle dates, manifests, signatures and selected relationships.
4. Version the Release cursor semantics. Old Release tokens that cannot establish the new guarantee must fail closed with a recoverable start-again response. Preserve unrelated cursor behavior and the supported 1–100 page-size contract.
5. State PostgreSQL and SQLite behavior explicitly. PostgreSQL is mandatory provider evidence. Prefer equivalent Release membership behavior in SQLite through bounded translated queries; do not silently describe SQLite tests as PostgreSQL proof.
6. A different mechanism is acceptable if it proves the same guarantee with less risk. A database-materialized membership design must justify its write/storage/expiry/cleanup costs. Do not add a general snapshot service, candidate-ID arrays in cursors, unbounded application-memory loading, or a long-lived MVCC transaction for this picker.

GLM must submit the selected design, alternatives rejected, proof of concurrency ordering, migration/legacy policy, exact file ownership and test plan to Astra **before production implementation or a committed migration**. Changes in controlled-history policy or an unexpectedly broad locking/schema change require renewed decision review.

## Acceptance

- [ ] **R01 — Baseline proof:** reproduce on an owned disposable PostgreSQL instance. Retain the exact SHA, Project/Release IDs, page-one response/cursor and unexpected continuation membership. Demonstrate the current after-cursor insertion defect.
- [ ] **R02 — Frozen membership:** multiple pages return every original matching candidate exactly once and no later insertion, including insertions before/after the cursor and with/without a search term. A new first-page traversal includes the newly committed matching builds.
- [ ] **R03 — Real concurrency:** deterministic barriers exercise a writer begun before page one and committed later, two writers committing in a different order where the design allows it, and rollback. Prove the selected fence's boundary and bounded cancellation/timeout behavior; sleeps alone are not the concurrency proof.
- [ ] **R04 — Historical integrity and upgrade:** qualify empty-database installation and upgrade from the preceding main schema with released/in-work and legacy/null-canonical rows. All remain selectable in canonical order. Compare original controlled columns, representative relationship identities and stored manifest/signature bytes before/after. Reapplying the supported migration/startup path is idempotent.
- [ ] **R05 — Every insertion path:** prove normal creation, import acceptance and project setup cannot bypass membership assignment. Inventory seed/repository/bulk paths and qualify their shared enforcement, including old-writer compatibility if the rollout permits mixed versions. Operational watermark changes cannot be silently rewritten.
- [ ] **R06 — Cursor and access boundaries:** reject malformed/unsupported/old Release tokens and wrong Project/type/search/order contracts. Preserve page-size limits. Revoked/foreign-project access is denied on continuation and relationship write. Define bounded cursor parsing and any expiry without changing unrelated histories.
- [ ] **R07 — Existing behavior:** retain canonical numeric ordering (including 9.0 before 10.5), historical labels/ties, exact selected Release IDs/deep links, released and in-work candidates, project-wide document semantics and existing non-Release relationship paging.
- [ ] **R08 — Bounded execution:** query filtering and continuation run in the database before materialization, with at most pageSize+1 candidates loaded. Retain PostgreSQL SQL/query-plan and representative size/latency evidence. State cost and lock contention honestly; no universal index-only or constant database-work claim.
- [ ] **R09 — Provider and browser proof:** mandatory PostgreSQL tests actually execute with none skipped. Record SQLite behavior separately. A focused real-client journey loads another page, refreshes/reopens the picker and saves a relationship to the exact selected build on disposable state; mocks alone do not prove the provider behavior.
- [ ] **R10 — Contracts and qualification:** update the documented Release exception to the guarantee actually implemented. Update architecture/state only where materially warranted; append any required decision rather than rewriting history. Run the changed-area planner, selected generators twice with a stable second result, required build/tests and documentation guard. Ensure new PostgreSQL cases are included in a required runner rather than an unselected/skipped class.
- [ ] **R11 — Protected integration and rollout:** obtain Astra's final-head review, exact-head Full Product/trusted readiness, integration-readiness review and protected composed-candidate checks. Inspect automatic HOME rollout behavior before queue admission; use the supported backup/isolated-copy/upgrade path for schema deployment.
- [ ] **R12 — Whole-issue completion:** record merged main, target runtime source/migration identity and focused post-deployment read acceptance. No persistent test inserts, resets or reseeding. Keep the issue open until Astra accepts the complete evidence; if rollout is blocked, report that boundary explicitly.

## Supervised GLM checkpoints

**A — Diagnosis/design**, before production edits or migration implementation.  
**B — Core snapshot and migration proof**, before treating the design as qualified.  
**C — Final implementation**, before applying `ready-for-full-ci`.  
**D — Green-head integration and rollout readiness**, before enabling auto-merge/queue admission.  
**E — Post-merge acceptance**, before closing #1040.

Each packet identifies the full immutable base/head SHA, worktree/PR, changed files, issue acceptance map, exact commands/results, provider/database/evidence identity, actual inspected artifacts, limitations and recommended next action. Astra returns **PASS**, **CHANGES REQUIRED**, or **NOT REVIEWABLE**, with explicit scope. GLM must stop the gated work and wait for real Astra feedback relayed by the owner. Never simulate approval, treat elapsed time as approval, or carry a PASS onto a changed head.

Persistent PostgreSQL `127.0.0.1:54329/aerolink`, `product/.local`, other worktrees and controlled history remain protected. Use one owned isolated branch, current repository contracts and current `product/docs/MERGING.md`. Stop after this issue is completely accepted.

## Independent review, 2026-09-15 — still live at current main, and the fix needs a schema decision

Re-verified read-only against protected main `966c2c256d1444a4f77b431ba20ae613643af4fa`. Main has advanced past the `77eab32c` cited in the body; #1038, #1046/#1050 and #1052 have merged since.

**Confirmed still present.** In `product/src/AeroLink.Api/ManagedDocumentEndpoints.cs`, every candidate branch except Release applies the snapshot predicate:

    if (db.Database.IsNpgsql()) query = query.Where(x => x.CreatedAt <= snapshotAt);

That line is present in the `SystemChangeRequest`, `ProblemReport` and `TestChangeRequest` branches. The `Release` branch (around lines 857-865) has no equivalent — it filters by project and term, applies `SoftwareReleaseOrderingQuery.WithSortKey`, and pages by `SortKey` only. `snapshotAt` is still threaded into `LinkOptionPage` for the Release branch, so the response carries a snapshot value it never enforced.

**Root cause confirmed.** `SoftwareRelease` (`product/src/AeroLink.Domain/Programs/ProgramRecord.cs`) exposes `Id`, `ProjectId`, `Version`, `CanonicalIdentity`, `PredecessorReleaseId`, `IsReleased`, `ReleasedAt`. There is **no** `CreatedAt`, so the predicate has nothing to filter on. `Id` is a random `Guid` and `ReleasedAt` is null for in-work builds, so neither is a usable creation-order surrogate.

**Two design points the body leaves open:**

1. **Backfill policy.** Adding `CreatedAt` needs a decision for existing rows. There is a direct in-repo precedent on the same entity — `CanonicalIdentity`'s doc comment: *"Historical rows may be null until an explicit, audited migration backfills them; raw Version is never rewritten in that process."* Recommend the same shape: nullable column, historical rows null, explicit audited backfill, original facts never rewritten. A blanket `now()` backfill would make every historical release sort as newer than any snapshot taken before the migration, quietly breaking the guarantee it is meant to create.

2. **Provider asymmetry.** The existing snapshot is `IsNpgsql()`-gated, so SQLite paths have never had frozen paging. Decide explicitly whether the Release fix matches that asymmetry or closes it, and record the choice — otherwise a SQLite-backed test can pass while proving nothing about the guarantee.

**Sequencing dependency on #1041.** The acceptance here requires PostgreSQL qualification. #1041 is the defect that makes the changed-area planner's cleanup proof fail under Windows PowerShell 5.1 during exactly that PostgreSQL work. Land #1041 first, or this issue's PostgreSQL evidence has to be produced under PowerShell 7 with the scope explicitly recorded.

**Recommend keeping this in its own PR.** It is the only one of #1040/#1041/#1043/#1053 that touches controlled domain data and adds a migration; the other three are tooling and operations. Combining a schema change with production-updater changes couples schema risk to runtime-restart risk in the same rollout — and those updater fixes exist precisely because that rollout path is fragile. It also destroys revert granularity: a picker-snapshot problem should be revertible without reverting the fixes keeping HOME alive.

title: Freeze Release relationship-picker candidates across cursor pages
